Fo bo with a star
Jul 2025 • Solo
After a long walk, I was looking for a place to finally eat, and on the map I came across this place simply called Pho. What else do you need on your first day in Vietnam but a plate of hot Pho Bo? Especially at the entrance are painted Michelin signs - solid, it is no longer possible to pass by. The place is small: several tables and a kitchen in plain sight. It later turned out there was a second room just down the street. The menu is extensive, with pictures and English translation, so it's convenient to order. Prices are nice. The service is quick - ten minutes after the order I was already facing a big bowl of my Fo Bo. The portion is generous: lots of meat, rich broth, fresh vegetables served separately, sauces on the table. Branded dishes are small, but nice. The soup turned out to be delicious and satisfying. Exactly what it takes to officially consider a day in Vietnam a success.

Pho
Apr 2024 • Friends
We hadn't had Pho yet on our trip so decided on Pho Viet Nam as it was close and on the Michelin guide. We walked in and ordered the Pho To Ba C5, as there was a little stamp next to it that said "Best Seller."

It was a mix of beef shank, flank, oxtail, and beef ribs. Meat lovers paradise really.

We were unaware that the pho came in a hot stone bowl, with the water literally boiling ahahah. Tbf it did say that on the menu, but I just saw the best seller stamp and let it fly. I would have ordered something else as it was 38 degrees (100 F) outside, but that's on me.

I dumped the rare beef, thick rice noodles, bean sprouts, and green onions into the sizzling bowl and waited about 5 minutes before I touched it because it was that hot.

The bowl was good, but I have to imagine that at that temperature some of the flavor of the broth gets lost. I found it to be a little bland, but adding some chili oil definitely helped. Also, the rice noodles kind of got cooked to a crisp and started falling apart, so it became hard to eat them.

Wish I could have got back to try a non boiling bowl, but just didn't have the time.

To be honest, The Michelin Guide was pretty hit or miss for me in Vietnam as I had much better success asking locals for recommendations. Really makes you wonder..........

Partly top, partly flop
Nov 2023 • Couples
We ate here twice. Meat in soup tastes good, but only if you get the slightly more expensive version in the stone bowl. This way you can add the raw meat to the soup yourself until it is cooked to your desired level and it can be eaten tender. On the second visit I accidentally ordered the normal Pho with raw beef, but when it arrived the meat had probably been in there for a while and was as tough as a shoe sole. 
The soup itself is relatively low in salt and has hardly any flavor. But you can spice it up with lots of fresh herbs. The sprouts served with it were a total no-go, they were unappetizingly brown and anything but fresh. 
The restaurant is very busy, especially in the evenings, and the food is served quickly. 
But this year's Michelin award has gone to the owner's head. In the kitchen, which is visible, she pulls a face like 10 days of rainy weather. 
Unfortunately, it's not a place to feel comfortable.

Best phở joint in Vietnam?
May 2023 • Couples
We found this place by accident, as it’s not centrally located and has such an unimaginative name. It was such a pleasant surprise, as this is undoubtedly among the best phở in Vietnam! Go for the house special; the delicious pho broth and cooked meat (which includes brisket and oxtail) is served in stone bowls, so remains piping hot for almost the whole meal. You can order extra sides, like tendon, blood, an egg, etc, but sadly no tripes. The raw meat and noodles come separately, and you throw them into the bowl. Unique among phở restaurants anywhere in the world, they make their noodles fresh from scratch here, and you can observe the whole process through the glass window. Boy, it makes a difference, freshly-made noodles are much, much better than the packaged dry ones served elsewhere. Crispy yu-tiao (extra price) is left on the table; I highly recommend you dip it in the broth for additional delish texture. Service is excellent, they’re super quick at bringing you requests for extra stuff, like fresh lime, etc. Our go-to

I don't understand the good reviews.
Dec 2022
Is this supposed to be good pho? Could the service be more notorious? I've been known to put up with bad service for good food but to have bad food and horrendous service??? I DON'T THINK SO!

First off, I was very excited to try Pho Viet Nam thanks to youtube influencers but I have to say they are so wrong about this spot. 

The pho was below average. The meat was not tender nor was it fresh. The soup was bland and not clean tasting. This pho simply does not do pho justice and is a disgrace to what pho really should be and is. I'm warning you, this is not real pho. 

As for the horrible and rude service, as soon as my husband and I stepped it we were greeted by an attitude because the waiter did not say one word to us but tossed us our menus on the table and stood there expecting us to order immediately. When I asked for a minute he gave me attitude and stood there waiting for our orders still. Okay, I can rush myself and order quickly, no problem. Then the waiter proceeds to take our menus and then brings to our table wet naps and some kind of dried fried bread that we DID NOT as for, without even saying a word. We just assumed it was free which was maybe our mistake? But I honestly think it was a trickery to charge our bill even more. 

Anyway, when we received out pho, our soup was luke-warm and wasn't nicely fragrant. I was so disappointed because youtubers were raving about this pho! So to add some flavor and i love some spice, I asked the waiter for hoison sauce and hot sauce. He completely decided to give me attitude, a dirty look, and proceeded to ignore me. I decided to ask again and without responding he walked to the kitchen and walked out with the sauces and in Vietnamese said, "here's the sauces you wanted."
